nonclaims: novelty of the classical rotor-router orbit theorem or Markov-chain tree theorem
a sandpile-group translation model, sink stabilization, or critical-group torsor

a rational-prime or prime-power orbit correspondence

source_lock.arithmetic_origin: directed spanning-tree and Laplacian data only; no rational-prime or prime-power orbit correspondence is intrinsic
source_lock.clock: one rotor advance and chip move
source_lock.determinant_convention: finite permutation determinant det(I-zU); Artin--Mazur zeta is its reciprocal
source_lock.family: every finite nonempty strongly connected directed multigraph with distinguished arcs and a cyclic order at each vertex
source_lock.forbidden_data: prime tables, target zeros or divisors, arithmetic local factors, Euler factors, root numbers, automorphy, Hilbert--Polya, and Route B
source_lock.forbidden_recast: no sink, stabilization, recurrent sandpile torsor, or critical-group translation is used
source_lock.state: a chip vertex and one currently selected outgoing arc at every vertex
source_lock.step: advance the chip-vertex rotor, then move the chip along the newly selected arc

theorem.arborescences: t_v is the number of directed spanning in-arborescences oriented toward v
theorem.eulerian: if the digraph is Eulerian then t_v=tau, M=tau, L=|E|, and every arc is traversed once per orbit
theorem.fixed_counts: #Fix(R^n)=M*L if L divides n and 0 otherwise
theorem.orbit_classification: the recurrent unicycle permutation has exactly M orbits, every one of exact length L
theorem.spectrum: every L-th root of unity occurs with multiplicity M
theorem.visits: each orbit visits v exactly d_v^+ t_v/M times and traverses each distinguished outgoing arc at v exactly t_v/M times
